stories.headline: Democrats vow to end Iran war as US midterm defeat hits Trump; oil prices fall
stories.title: Democrats vow to end Iran war as US midterm defeat hits Trump; oil prices fall
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 5: The Democrats have vowed to make ending the Iran war a priority after their sweeping victory in the US midterm elections, dealing a major political setback to President Donald Trump and his Republican Party, reports BBC. Democratic Senate leader Chuck Schumer said ending the conflict would be a priority, adding that cutting off funding to the Department of Defence could be considered if it was the only way to secure a swift end to the war. Hakeem Jeffries, the Democratic leader in the House of Representatives and likely to become the next Speaker, said his party would hold the Trump administration accountable and act as a check on what he described as an “out-of-control executive branch”. “We don’t work for Donald Trump. We don’t work for JD Vance. We don’t work for the Supreme Court. We work for the American people,” he said, according to the BBC. Jeffries also accused what he called the “Trump Cartel” of massive corruption, promising to hold those responsible accountable. The election outcome has also triggered a sharp fall in global oil prices, with crude touching its lowest level in two months amid expectations of renewed diplomatic engagement between the US and Iran. However, analysts feel that expectations might be premature, given the difficulties in negotiations between Washington and Tehran. Iran, he said, would seek “a top price” for fully reopening the Strait of Hormuz and allowing commercial shipping to move freely. The conflict had effectively closed the strategic waterway, through which around 20 per cent of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas normally passes, triggering a surge in global energy prices. Trump acknowledged that the Iran war was largely responsible for his party’s electoral defeat, while Vice-President JD Vance also said the conflict had contributed to the Republican setback. Russia, meanwhile, said the Democratic victory would not alter Washington’s foreign policy towards Ukraine. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Moscow would continue pursuing its interests either militarily or through negotiations. China has called for a “constructive, strategically stable China-US relationship” ahead of a planned meeting between Trump and President Xi Jinping this month. Beijing is expected to push for a trade agreement, with questions also emerging over whether Taiwan could figure in the negotiations. The Democratic victory has also raised questions about divisions within the party, particularly over Israel policy, which could complicate its efforts to shape the administration’s foreign and domestic agenda.

article_sentences: Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini on Friday (November 6, 2026) alleged that the AAP government in Punjab had spent elsewhere the ₹1,600 crore announced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi for the flood-hit State last year.

Mr. Saini said he had earlier watched a video on social media in which Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann had promised compensation for every loss suffered by people during the devastating floods, down to a single hen.
CM Mann had also said he did not need to look towards the Centre for funds, Mr. Saini said.

Mr. Saini further claimed that farmers from Punjab had told him that AAP ministers distributed compensation cheques in their presence and posed for photographs with the media, but took the cheques back after the media left.
"This is what they do.
Then how will the people of Punjab vote for them?" he asked.
Targeting CM Mann, Mr. Saini said the Punjab Chief Minister had spent five years cracking jokes instead of working.

stories.title: A man named Chris will be New Zealand's next prime minister, whichever party wins the election

article_sentences: Wellington (AP) New Zealand is choosing a new government in a national election that concludes Saturday.
But one outcome is already known: The next prime minister will be a man named Chris.
The leaders of the nation's two biggest political parties bear that name.
Center-right National is helmed by Christopher Luxon, who has been prime minister since the 2023 election, when his party ousted center-left Labour, led by Chris Hipkins.
Both leaders in the "battle of the Chrises" are, according to most opinion polls, fairly unpopular with voters.

The ascension of political Chrises is linked to the popularity of the name Christopher for New Zealand children until the mid-1980s, peaking in 1968 when nearly 800 babies were given the name, according to government data.
In 2025, just 20 newborns were named Christopher.
Here's how to tell the political leaders apart.
The National party's leader and incumbent prime minister, Luxon, 56, was one of more than 600 Christophers born in New Zealand in 1970.

Addressing a news conference, the IGP Kashmir identified the lone active local terrorist as Muhammed Lateef Bhat of Kulgam, who is linked to two terror attacks earlier this year - one in Anantnag that killed a police official and another in Kulgam in which two migrant workers from Chhattisgarh were shot dead. “There is certainly one local terrorist, supported by a few foreign terrorists. We have some footprints, but giving a fixed number of active terrorists would be an exaggeration because they are constantly moving from one place to another,” Kumar said. He said that there is no official data available on any infiltration this year. Kumar said security forces continue to track the group based on available inputs. Referring to recent encounters in Budgam, the IGP said the terrorists killed in two operations were shot dead in the upper reaches. The area connects with the Pir Panjal range and Kishtwar, terrain that has remained a focus of joint operations by the Army, J&K Police, and Central Armed Police Forces. Sustained domination of these high-altitude areas has enabled successful operations, he noted. On the technological capabilities of the terrorists, IGP Kashmir said said the gadgets they are using are under surveillance. “Whatever technology they are using is on our radar. We have devised a mechanism and will not allow their nefarious designs to succeed,” he said, while declining to share operational specifics. The IGP Kashmir also detailed security arrangements along the National Highway. He said that following a terror attack, a security mechanism was put in place and aligned along the highway. "Further realignment will be discussion with other agencies," Kumar said. “In Srinagar we get inputs, which is why extra measures have been put in place. Still, we recover IEDs around the National Highway - threats are there,” he said. About restrictions, the IGP Kashmir said that the matter would have to be discussed with other agencies. The remarks come amid ongoing implementation of the winter security strategy. stories.title: Dr Farooq Abdullah dismisses reports of NC split, says legislators' grievances genuine
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 06: National Conference president Farooq Abdullah on Friday dismissed reports of a possible split in the party as baseless, saying the concerns raised by around 16 legislators were genuine and would be addressed by the leadership. Speaking to reporters, after meeting the legislators, Dr Abdullah said the party leadership had listened to their grievances and would take steps to resolve them. "We have spoken to them. Their problems were genuine and they were heard properly. We will take some steps quickly and some steps slowly," he said. He said the party would work towards strengthening both the organisation and the government to ensure that people's problems were addressed. Dismissing speculation about a possible rebellion within the ruling party, Abdullah said the National Conference remained united and could not be divided. "The news that a split is taking place in the National Conference is completely baseless. This community is organised, and those who think they can break it should remember that it has never been broken and never will be," he said. The meeting comes amid reports of discontent among a section of NC legislators over the functioning of the party and the government. Around 16 MLAs had sought an interaction with the party leadership, triggering speculation about internal differences within the ruling party. Dr Farooq Abdullah also reiterated the party's commitment to seeking restoration of Jammu and Kashmir's statehood and Article 370. "Our fight for the restoration of statehood will continue. Our fight for Article 370 and Article 35A will also continue, and, God willing, we will take the matter to the Supreme Court," he said. The National Conference had made restoration of Jammu and Kashmir's special status and statehood key promises in its 2024 Assembly election manifesto. The Supreme Court had upheld the Centre's August 2019 decision to abrogate Article 370 in December 2023, while directing that Assembly elections be held in Jammu and Kashmir and statehood be restored at the earliest. The NC-led government, headed by Chief Minister Omar Abdullah, assumed office in October 2024 after the party emerged as the single largest party in the Assembly elections. (KNS)

The Court clarified that the judgment was applicable to the parties before the Court and that seniority and promotions would not be reopened.
The pending cases will be decided by the courts on their own merits and entitlement.

The Applicant therefore respectfully submits that the temporal operation of the Judgment requires clarification so as to avoid unsettling completed selections, appointments and admissions and the consequential rights arising therefrom”, the plea states.

The Centre had sought two years to establish equivalence of posts in other organisations with government posts after consultations with the concerned stakeholders and to formulate a uniform mechanism for determining OBC creamy-layer status where equivalence has not been established.

The Centre had also sought permission to finalise service allocation for 958 candidates recommended by the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) in the Civil Services Examination (CSE) 2025, pending a decision on the clarification application.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Expresses Pain Over Death Of Girl Due To School Pillar Collapse, Quashes Criminal Case Against Officer-Bearers
stories.title: Supreme Court Expresses Pain Over Death Of Girl Due To School Pillar Collapse, Quashes Criminal Case Against Officer-Bearers
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: A bench of Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice Manmohan quashed the proceedings, allowing the appeal against the Bombay High Court's order by which it had refused to quash it.
The deceased was a Class 7 student aged 12 who met with an accident within the school premises when a pillar under construction collapsed and fell on her, resulting in severe fatal injuries.
The incident happened on February 15, 2020 in a school in Amaravati District.

A case was subsequently filed by the deceased girl's father alleging that the school's director and the hostel superintendent deliberately made the kaccha and standardless construction of the pillar and did not take the precautions while constructing the pillar.
The appellants were thereafter prosecuted under Section 304 read with Section 34 of the IPC (now Section 105 and Section 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023/BNS respectively).
The appellants approached the High Court seeking quashing of the case against them.

However, the High Court refused to quash the proceedings, relying on a Chemical Analyser's report, which showed that the cement-sand-aggregate ratio in the mortar was not maintained, and on the spot panchnama, which said the pillar had no solid base.

It further held that there was a breach of duty and that “though there was no intention to cause death but admittedly knowledge was there that sub standard material while constructing the base for installation of pillar may cause harm or death to the person.”
Aggrieved by the High Court's refusal, the appellants approached the Supreme Court.
Before the Supreme Court, the appellants argued that no voluntary commission of an offence was made out in the prosecution's case, therefore, Section 304 of the IPC would not apply.
It was also submitted that Section 304A of the IPC would also not apply because the appellants' lack of care could be one of the causes of death, but not the direct consequence.
For context, Section 304 of the IPC deals with the offence of culpable homicide not amounting to murder, and Section 304A deals with the offence of death caused by negligent act.

stories.title: Madhya Pradesh cabinet approves ₹63,296 crore plan for five greenfield corridors
stories.summary: MP is developing a modern road network through the construction of state highways, four-lane, six-lane and eight-lane roads, as well as greenfield expressways: CM Mohan Yadav
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet approves' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Madhya Pradesh government is moving ahead with a plan to build five greenfield expressway corridors across the state at an estimated cost of ₹63,296 crore.
The decision was reviewed at the 49th board meeting of the Madhya Pradesh Road Development Corporation (MPRDC), chaired by Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav on Thursday.
The proposed four-lane, access-controlled corridors will span a total length of 1,398 km.
They include Bhopal–Mandsaur (258 km), Sagar–Satna (227 km), Jabalpur–Ashapur (358 km), Bhopal–Gwalior (320 km) and Katni–Singrauli (235 km).
Feasibility reports for the first three corridors are being prepared, with consultants submitting alignment options for review.
For the Bhopal–Gwalior and Katni–Singrauli routes, the tender process for selecting DPR consultants is underway.
CM Yadav directed officials to expedite ongoing road projects and stressed that no village, town or city should remain deprived of all-weather road connectivity.
He also renamed the corporation’s proposed Highway Fund as the ‘Viksit Madhya Pradesh Sankalp Path’.

The board approved several key decisions, including 100% divestment of equity in the four-lane Jaora–Nayagaon BOT project, creation of new senior posts, acquisition of the PAM Building in Bhopal, and exemption of combine harvesters from toll charges at all MPRDC-operated plazas.

stories.headline: Videocon founder Venugopal Dhoot declared bankrupt by NCLT
stories.title: Videocon founder Venugopal Dhoot declared bankrupt by NCLT
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 6 : The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) has declared former Videocon Industries promoter Venugopal Nandlal Dhoot bankrupt after admitting a petition filed by State Bank of India (SBI) to recover dues of more than Rs 12,668 crore arising from personal guarantees furnished for loans extended to Videocon group companies. A Mumbai bench of the tribunal admitted SBI's petition under Section 123 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), paving the way for bankruptcy proceedings against Dhoot as a personal guarantor. The order follows the failure of his personal insolvency resolution process after creditors rejected a proposed repayment plan. The tribunal appointed insolvency professional Asish Narayan as bankruptcy trustee and directed that Dhoot's estate be vested in him for administration and distribution among creditors. According to the PSU lender, Dhoot's outstanding liabilities stood at Rs 12,668.06 crore, including interest and penalties as of September 30. The dues relate to personal guarantees provided by Dhoot for term loans, working capital facilities and borrowings extended to Videocon Group entities, including Videocon Telecommunications Ltd. The lender had invoked the guarantees in February 2018 following loan defaults by the group. During the personal insolvency proceedings, Dhoot proposed a repayment plan offering Rs 600 crore over three years through a proposed real estate development project in Siliguri. The amount represented less than 1 per cent of the admitted claims. However, the resolution professional flagged concerns over the proposal and said that it was dependent on future project approvals and uncertain cash flows and did not provide any upfront payment. Creditors subsequently declined to approve the plan. The tribunal terminated the insolvency resolution process in July this year and allowed creditors to initiate bankruptcy proceedings. SBI filed its bankruptcy petition within the prescribed timeline thereafter. Moreover, the bankruptcy trustee has been directed to invite claims from creditors, take control of Dhoot's estate and submit a preliminary report to the tribunal within 90 days. --IANS
